title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Π̂_{0,3} is the profinite fundamental group of P^1−{0,1,∞}, i.e. the free profinite group of rank 2. Ŝ^+_{0,3} is the profinite orbifold fundamental group of the quotient [(P^1−{0,1,∞})/S_3]. It sits in the exact sequence (31) 1→Π̂_{0,3}→Ŝ^+_{0,3}→S_3→1 from the previous page. The previous page showed the following: the outer automorphisms of Ŝ^+ that preserve Π̂ and are trivial on S_3 correspond to automorphisms inducing the identity on S_3, taken modulo inner automorphisms by elements of Π̂. The page asks whether such an automorphism is determined by its restriction to Π̂.

Step 1 (injectivity). Let f ∈ Aut(Ŝ^+) induce the identity on both Π̂ and S_3. Lift the transposition σ_∞ to Ŝ^+; then f(σ_∞) = σ_∞·g with g ∈ Π̂. He notes in passing that order 2 is preserved, so (σ_∞ g)^2 = 1, i.e. g·σ_∞(g) = 1; this is not needed. Since f fixes Π̂ pointwise, for x ∈ Π̂ we have σ_∞xσ_∞^{-1} = f(σ_∞xσ_∞^{-1}) = (σ_∞g)x(σ_∞g)^{-1}. Hence int(g)|Π̂ = id, so g lies in the centre of Π̂. The centre of a free profinite group of rank ≥2 is trivial, so g = 1. Thus f is the identity on Π̂·⟨σ̂_∞⟩, the preimage of {1,σ_∞}. By symmetry the same holds for σ_0 and σ_1. The three preimages generate Ŝ^+ (two would already suffice, since two transpositions generate S_3), so f = id. In modern terms: automorphisms trivial on N and on G/N correspond to 1-cocycles G/N→Z(N), and here Z(Π̂) = 1.

Step 2 (extension problem). Which automorphisms of Π̂ extend to automorphisms of Ŝ^+ inducing the identity on S_3? A necessary condition is that the induced outer automorphism commutes with the outer S_3-action. The next page proves sufficiency by the standard construction for extensions with centreless kernel. Call Γ the centralizer of S_3 in Out(Π̂). Then S_3×Γ embeds in Out(Π̂), which gives an extension E of S_3×Γ by Π̂, and hence an outer action of Γ on Ŝ^+. Conclusion: Γ ≅ {outer automorphisms of Ŝ^+_{0,3} inducing the trivial outer automorphism on S_3}.

Purpose. This is part of the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' and the Galois/Teichmüller programme. The aim is to describe the 'automorphisms of the Teichmüller tower' at level (0,3) intrinsically, either as S_3-equivariant outer automorphisms of F̂_2 or as outer automorphisms of profinite PSL_2(Z). GT̂ (and the image of Gal(Q̄/Q)) lives inside this group Γ.
errors: Ŝ^+_{0,3} is written as ≅ Sl(2,Z)^. The extension with kernel the free group Π̂_{0,3} and quotient S_3 is PSL(2,Z)^ (orbifold π1 of the j-line = λ-line/S_3). In SL(2,Z) the preimage of the transposition has order 4 and Γ(2) = F_2×{±1}. His own relation (σ_∞g)^2 = 1 is consistent with PSL, not SL. This is a minor slip, or SL used loosely.

The relation g·σ_∞(g) = 1 is irrelevant to the argument; the conclusion comes only from the triviality of the centre (in fact the centralizer) of Π̂. The phrase 'd'où g ∈' is left unfinished but corrected immediately below.
No substantive gap: the injectivity argument is correct.

ideas.what: An automorphism of an extension that is trivial on the kernel and the quotient is trivial when the kernel has trivial centre (here the centre of the free profinite group of rank 2 is trivial).
ideas.modern_name: Automorphisms of extensions / H^1(G/N, Z(N)); centre-freeness of free profinite groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical group theory (Schreier, Eilenberg–MacLane); centre-freeness of free profinite groups standard (e.g. Ribes–Zalesskii)
ideas.where_published: Similar centre-free arguments underlie the Esquisse d'un programme / Longue Marche discussion of outer actions, but no specific statement is known to me.

ideas.what: The profinite orbifold π1 of (P^1−{0,1,∞})/S_3 identified with profinite (P)SL_2(Z), as an extension of S_3 by F̂_2.
ideas.modern_name: π1 of the moduli stack M_{1,1} / j-line orbifold; Γ(2)\PSL_2(Z) ≅ S_3
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical; in the GT context Ihara, Lochak–Schneps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the role of SL_2(Z)^ and of M_{1,1} in the Teichmüller tower.

ideas.what: Outer automorphisms of profinite PSL_2(Z) trivial on S_3 correspond to S_3-equivariant (centralizing) outer automorphisms of F̂_2 (necessity here, sufficiency on the next page).
ideas.modern_name: Correspondence between outer actions and extensions with centreless kernel; centralizer of S_3 in Out(F̂_2), an ambient group containing GT̂
ideas.usually_credited_to: Group-theoretic part classical; in the GT context Drinfeld (1990), Ihara, Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura
ideas.where_published: Possibly sketched in La Longue Marche (1981); unsure.

deep.surprise_reason: Correct but routine group theory (centre-free kernel ⇒ automorphisms of the extension are determined by the outer action). It is a preparatory step toward describing automorphisms of the (0,3) level of the Teichmüller tower and is well covered by the later GT̂ literature. Nothing new.
transcription_corrections: 'Un {+ext[?]+} automorphisme': 'ext' is a superscript insertion above 'automorphisme', i.e. 'Un automorphisme ext.'; the question is about outer automorphisms.
The bracketed insertion '$\hat\Pi_{0,\infty}\cdot\{1,\hat\sigma_\infty\}$' should read $\hat\Pi_{0,3}\cdot\{1,\hat\sigma_\infty\}$ (preimage of {1,σ_∞}).
'$\dot\sigma_0,\dot\sigma_1$' are lifted (hatted/dotted) σ_0, σ_1, analogous to σ̂_∞.
'd'où g∈' is an abandoned fragment; the argument continues with 'int(g)|Π̂_{0,3} = id i.e. g ∈ Centre(Π̂_{0,3}) i.e. g=1'.
'[et on doit avoir σ_∞gσ_∞g=1 i.e. g·σ_∞(g)=1]': the bracket closes after g·σ_∞(g)=1, consistent with the image.
